headline: New AI Tool Accelerates mRNA-Based Treatments for Viruses, Cancers, Genetic Disorders
summary: UT Austin and Sanofi developed RiboNN, an AI model that predicts protein production from mRNA sequences and could help researchers design future therapies.
sourceOrganization: UT Austin · College of Natural Sciences
imageAlt: Colorful RNA illustration beside rows of nucleotide letters.
imageCredit: UT Austin College of Natural Sciences

headline: Meet the Universe’s Earliest Confirmed Black Hole: A Monster at the Dawn of Time
summary: A UT-led astronomy team used James Webb Space Telescope spectroscopy to confirm a black hole in CAPERS-LRD-z9, observed just 500 million years after the Big Bang.
imageAlt: Artist's illustration of a black hole surrounded by a glowing red and orange gas cloud.
imageCredit: Erik Zumalt, The University of Texas at Austin

headline: University of Texas-led Team Solves a Big Problem for Fusion Energy
summary: A new method predicts particle motion about ten times faster, helping engineers design magnetic confinement systems for fusion reactors while retaining accuracy.
sourceOrganization: UT Austin · College of Natural Sciences
imageAlt: Colored looping paths visualize predicted particle motions in a fusion reactor.
imageCredit: Max Ruth/University of Texas at Austin

headline: New Chemical Discovery Could Make Medicine and Manufacturing More Sustainable
summary: UT chemists developed a carbon-coupling method using sodium formate that avoids hazardous steps and could make chemical manufacturing more sustainable.
sourceOrganization: UT Austin · College of Natural Sciences
imageAlt: A metallic molecular model emerges between two halves of a turquoise and silver capsule.

headline: Research Identifies Key Antibodies for Development of Broadly Protective Norovirus Vaccine
summary: Researchers identified antibodies that neutralize diverse norovirus strains, offering clues for a broader vaccine and possible antibody treatments.
sourceOrganization: UT Austin · College of Natural Sciences
imageAlt: Blue norovirus particles illustrated against a pale background.

headline: Study Finds Early Signs of Widespread Coastal Marsh Decline
summary: A satellite-based model revealed declining root biomass along Georgia's coast, giving researchers an earlier warning of marsh deterioration.
sourceOrganization: UT Austin · College of Natural Sciences
imageAlt: Sunrise illuminates grass in a salt marsh on Sapelo Island, Georgia.
